hints: Each planet eventually repeats because every planet has exactly one outgoing link.
For every start, the number of distinct planets visited equals its distance to a cycle plus that cycle's length.
Find cycles, then propagate cycle length plus one backward through incoming trees.
analogy: Count the nonrepeating lead-in and add the loop length.
example: If a planet reaches a 3-planet cycle after two steps, it visits five distinct planets before repeating.
algorithm: Use DFS states or indegree peeling to identify cycles. Assign each cycle node its cycle length, then process reverse-tree nodes so answer[u]=answer[next[u]]+1.
correctness: A path from u consists of its unique tree path into a cycle plus every cycle node once; this recurrence counts exactly those distinct nodes.
